correctness.rationale: For every integer sample size, the almost-surely unique maximizing signed order-statistic deviation partitions the ordered-uniform simplex into disjoint events. Fixing its rank and location forces exact affine bands for all remaining ranks, whose volumes factor on the left and right. Splitting affine constraints at rational intersections yields constant bin eligibility and polynomial volumes from the exact ordered-simplex count recurrence; the CDF threshold has explicit quadratic radical endpoints. Integrating these polynomials exactly proves the finite algebraic CDF for all rational thresholds and piecewise algebraicity for all positive real thresholds. Direct low-n radical identities, strict rational 95% quantile enclosure, algebraic sign checks and 120 checker assertions confirm the implementation; seeded simulations independently agree but are not used to prove the theorem.

value.rationale: The source itself identifies the two-sided finite CDF as unavailable, while accurate finite-sample goodness-of-fit calibration is its central statistical motivation. The result closes this natural gap for all sample sizes with an exact algorithm (rather than a small arbitrary table), supplies radical closed values for small samples, and certifies a rigorous 5% finite-sample critical-value bracket.
